derivation_basis: Arithmetic derived from one-decimal PROJWT-weighted aggregate percentages; not recomputed from respondent-level microdata.

external_published_reference.publisher: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction

methodology.denominator: Population represented by adults who reported a disaster impact in the previous five years and were asked the advance-warning question; this is not all adults.
methodology.weight: Uses the publisher-aligned PROJWT-weighted aggregate percentages from the frozen reproduction record.
methodology.calculation: warned_and_able = round1(receipt * conditional_action / 100); warned_but_unable = round1(receipt - warned_and_able); not_warned = round1(100 - receipt).
methodology.rounding: Inputs are already rounded to one decimal place. Residual allocation makes displayed categories sum to 100.0; components are approximate, not exact underlying population estimates.

interpretation.statement: The decomposition makes the conditional warning-to-action gap visible on a common per-100-impacted-adults denominator. It does not identify why people could not act or estimate protective actions verified by independent event records.

limitations: The inputs are one-decimal rounded estimates; derived components are approximate and rounding residual is assigned to warned-but-unable.
No design-based confidence intervals or effective sample sizes are calculated.
The survey is retrospective and self-reported; warning receipt, comprehension, feasibility, verified action and avoided loss are distinct constructs.
The result is global and must not be interpreted as a Georgia national estimate; Georgia's warning-question base is 99.
This is arithmetic on an existing frozen aggregate record, not a new survey or a second raw-microdata reproduction.
